title: Money Primitives Demonstrator
description: Demonstrator node for the shared _money.bundle.mjs kernel: exact decimal parse at a caller-declared scale (closed grammar; exponent form, thousands separators and excess precision are named refusals), BigInt minor-unit arithmetic with no engine float on the value path, six named rounding modes in a closed set with structured refusal on unknown or missing tokens, single-rounding mul and div with a zero-divisor refusal, largest-remainder allocation whose parts sum exactly, and receipt-form strings. Rounds a caller-supplied amount to the currency exponent (or explicit places) with the required mode, allocates across integer weights, and echoes the mode. Currency exponents arrive as data via policy_parameters.currency_slice; the fixture slice reflects ISO 4217 Amendment 180 (BGN historic for Bulgaria from 2026-01-01, EUR effective).

amount.description: Exact decimal amount, grammar -?digits(.digits)? at the currency exponent. Exponent form, thousands separators, empty input and excess fractional digits are named refusals (REFUSED_MONEY_PARSE / REFUSED_MONEY_PRECISION) unless truncate_excess is declared.

ccy.description: 3-letter uppercase ISO 4217 code; must be present in the caller-supplied currency_slice.

mode.description: REQUIRED rounding mode from the closed set. Unknown or missing tokens are REFUSED_UNKNOWN_ROUNDING_MODE, never a fallback.

weights.description: Non-empty allocation weights (safe integers <= 1e15); largest-remainder parts sum exactly to the rounded amount.

currency_slice.description: Currency exponents as DATA: { table_version, currencies: [{ ccy, exponent (0..4 or null), status?, valid_from?, valid_to? }] }, 1..64 entries. The kernel bakes no exponents.

places.description: Optional rounding target; defaults to the currency exponent.

truncate_excess.description: DECLARED truncation flag: allow parse-time truncation of fractional digits beyond the currency exponent (toward zero). Default false.

mcp_tool_definition.name: money_primitives_demo
mcp_tool_definition.description: Rounds a caller-supplied exact-decimal amount to the currency exponent with one required named rounding mode from a closed six-token set, allocates the rounded amount across integer weights by largest remainder (parts sum exactly), and echoes the mode and matched currency-slice entry. Currency exponents are caller data; malformed input yields a named refusal, never a silent zero or fallback.

source: authored by SHARED-MONEY-BUNDLE-1 per ACCT-INFRA-KERNELS-BUILD-SPEC.md §0.1/§1.4/§4.1 and the browser-first-primitives review (defects D7/D8/D9/D11). ISO 4217 state per Amendment 180 (SIX, published 2025-09-22): as of 2026-01-01 the Bulgarian lev is historic for Bulgaria and the euro is effective. Rounding-mode semantics follow the widely-recognised Java RoundingMode naming (behaviour definition, cited in kernel source only as the closed-set contract).
author: PostOakLabs

output_example.message: parsed at the currency exponent, rounded once with the required mode, allocated by largest remainder (parts sum exactly)
output_example.scope_note: Demonstrator for the _money shared bundle: strict decimal parse at the currency exponent, one rounding with a required named mode from the closed set {half_up, half_down, half_even, truncate, floor, ceiling}, and largest-remainder allocation whose parts sum exactly. No FX, no float math, no default mode. Currency exponents are caller data (policy_parameters.currency_slice), never kernel bytes. Not a migration target: existing sealed kernels are out of scope by row fence.
